theory.intro: When a particle's velocity changes with time, questions ask **when** something happens. The particle is momentarily **at rest** only when both components of $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ are zero at the same time; it moves parallel to an axis when just one component is zero.
facts: A particle is at rest when $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}=0$ at the same value of $t$.
If only $\dot{y}=0$, the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis, not at rest.
Speed is $|\underset{\sim}{v}|=\sqrt{\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}}$, so it is never negative and is never $\dot{x}+\dot{y}$.
Since the square root is increasing, minimise or maximise $\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}$ instead of the speed itself.
Solve each component equation separately, then keep only the times common to both.
Reject any solution with $t<0$, or outside the interval the question states.
Substitute the time back into $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ to find where the event happens.
steps: Write the condition described in the question as equations in $\dot{x}$ and $\dot{y}$
Solve for $t$, rejecting times outside the allowed interval
Substitute that value of $t$ back to answer the question asked

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-6t+5)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t+8)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is momentarily at rest.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
Both components vanish at $t=3$, so the particle is at rest at $t=3$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-12t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is momentarily at rest.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-12)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3t^{2}-12=0$
$t^{2}=4$
$t=2$ (rejecting $t=-2$ since $t\ge 0$)
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
Both components vanish at $t=2$, so the particle is at rest at $t=2$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{2}-10t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-3t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(4t-10)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Moving parallel to the $y$-axis means $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}\ne 0$.
$4t-10=0$
$t=2.5$
$\dot{y}(2.5)$
$=3(2.5)^{2}-6(2.5)$
$=18.75-15$
$=3.75$
Since $\dot{y}\ne 0$, the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis at $t=2.5$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(4t+1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=4\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Moving parallel to the $x$-axis means $\dot{y}=0$ and $\dot{x}\ne 0$.
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
$\dot{x}=4$, which is never zero, so the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis at $t=3$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{i}+4t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its minimum speed.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=(2t-6)^{2}+16$
The square root is increasing, so the speed is least when $(2t-6)^{2}$ is least.
$(2t-6)^{2}=0$
$t=3$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(3)|$
$=\sqrt{0+16}$
$=4$

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-3t^{2})\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t^{3}-6t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t>0$.
Find its position vector at the instant it is momentarily at rest.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{3}-9t^{2}+12t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-4t+4)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Show that the particle is momentarily at rest exactly once, and find that time.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(6t^{2}-18t+12)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$6t^{2}-18t+12=0$
$6(t-1)(t-2)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=2$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
Only $t=2$ makes both components zero, so the particle is at rest exactly once, at $t=2$.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+2t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0\le t\le \pi$.
Find all times at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=2\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\dot{y}=2$, which is never zero.
$2\cos 2t=0$
For $0\le t\le \pi$, $2t$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$.
$2t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ or $2t=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$
$t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $t=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0\le t\le 4$.
Find its minimum speed, in exact form.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=4t^{2}+(2t-6)^{2}$
$=4t^{2}+4t^{2}-24t+36$
$=8t^{2}-24t+36$
This is least at the vertex.
$t=\dfrac{24}{16}$
$t=1.5$, which lies in $0\le t\le 4$.
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(1.5)|^{2}$
$=8(2.25)-36+36$
$=18$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(1.5)|$
$=\sqrt{18}$
$=3\sqrt{2}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-6t^{2}+9t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t+5)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its position vector at the instant it is momentarily at rest.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-12t+9)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3(t-1)(t-3)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=3$
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
Both components vanish only at $t=3$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(3)$
$=(27-54+27)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9-18+5)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=0\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-4\underset{\sim}{j}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-4t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-27t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Is the particle ever momentarily at rest?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-27)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
$3t^{2}-27=0$
$t^{2}=9$
$t=3$ (rejecting $t=-3$ since $t\ge 0$)
The two components are never zero at the same time.
The particle is never at rest: at $t=2$ it is moving parallel to the $y$-axis, and at $t=3$ it is moving parallel to the $x$-axis.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(e^{t}-3t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the exact time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(e^{t}-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$e^{t}-3=0$
$e^{t}=3$
$t=\ln 3$
$\dot{y}(\ln 3)$
$=2\ln 3-2$
Since $\ln 3>1$, $\dot{y}\ne 0$, so the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis at $t=\ln 3$.

development.question_text:
A drone's position, in kilometres from its base, is $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=4t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$, where $t$ is in hours and $0\le t\le 4$.
Find its exact maximum speed over this interval.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=4\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=16+(2t-2)^{2}$
This is greatest when $(2t-2)^{2}$ is greatest, so test the ends of $0\le t\le 4$.
$(2(0)-2)^{2}=4$
$(2(4)-2)^{2}=36$
The maximum is at $t=4$.
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(4)|$
$=\sqrt{16+36}$
$=\sqrt{52}$
$=2\sqrt{13}$ km/h

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{3}-15t^{2}+24t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-8t+12)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its exact distance from the origin at the instant it is momentarily at rest.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(6t^{2}-30t+24)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-8)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$6(t-1)(t-4)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=4$
$2t-8=0$
$t=4$
Both components vanish only at $t=4$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(4)$
$=(128-240+96)\underset{\sim}{i}+(16-32+12)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-16\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{r}(4)|$
$=\sqrt{256+16}$
$=\sqrt{272}$
$=4\sqrt{17}$

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\left(t-4\ln(t+1)\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+5t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its minimum speed and the time at which it occurs.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=\left(1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=\left(1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}\right)^{2}+25$
The speed is least when the squared bracket is zero.
$1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}=0$
$t+1=4$
$t=3$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(3)|$
$=\sqrt{0+25}$
$=5$
The minimum speed is $5$, at $t=3$.

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}+at)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}+bt)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
The particle is momentarily at rest when $t=2$.
Find $a$ and $b$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t+a)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}+b)\underset{\sim}{j}$
At rest at $t=2$ means both components are zero there.
$4+a=0$
$a=-4$
$12+b=0$
$b=-12$
